segments.english: And how can we leave all the divinities that are above the World of Emanation, and worship specifically Ze'ir and his Nukva, who are in the World of Emanation, since there have already preceded him several Atikin and Arikhei Anpin, and Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva in the upper worlds; there is no number of those still closer to Ein Sof?

tokens.note: Ze'ir Anpin, 'Small Face' (Aramaic); here the bare name Ze'ir.
Nukva: the female partzuf paired with Ze'ir; 'his Nukva' carries the Hebrew possessive suffix.
Atik, plural Atikin: partzufim named for the Ancient One. Atika Kadisha is the Holy Ancient One.
Arikh Anpin, plural Arikhei Anpin: 'Long Face'.
Abba (Father) and Imma (Mother), written with the abbreviation ואו"א.
Ein Sof, literally 'without end'.
יותר: comparative with הקרובים לאין סוף, "closer to Ein Sof still / even closer": the questioner says there are countless partzufim nearer to Ein Sof than Ze'ir.

grammar: נניח and ונעבוד are first-person plural imperfects (not cohortatives, which would end in ה) in a rhetorical question: 'how shall we leave ... and worship'; the English reads 'can we leave'.
קדמו לו כמה עתיקין: the verb comes before its subject (verb-subject order), and לו means 'before him'.

The last clause, אין מספר הקרובים לאין סוף יותר?, means 'there is no number of those still closer to Ein Sof?': יותר is the comparative of הקרובים ('closer'), not 'and more'. The question mark is the Hebrew's.
segments.note: The questioner's letter, in his voice. Ze'ir and his Nukva are named as the partzufim the question asks us to worship.
apparatus: Wikisource base text; not yet collated with the 1931 scan (decisions, Q2).
ואו"א is one abbreviated word for Abba and Imma.

segments.english: And our early rabbis said that it is not fitting to worship, to give thanks, to magnify, and to glorify, except to the first God of all that exists apart from Him! And why should we leave the principal Ein Sof, that contracts above all of them, with all the partzufim close to it, and worship that which is very far from it, which is the last partzuf of the World of Emanation? All this, make us understand, our lord, let us go and pursue the LORD our Maker the Creator of the beginning. And do not pour upon us a word of Belial, God forbid. For who has gathered grace and good understanding in his palms, to have insight and to know the LORD through investigating divine matters in the principles of the faith, like you. Who will ascend to the mountain of the LORD, and who will stand in His holy place, like you, for I am more brutish than any man, and I have no understanding of a man. And the Rock knows the secrets of the heart, the examiner of hearts, for I did not give sleep to my eyes, and my sleep was taken from my eyes until I find solutions and whoever comes to purify himself, they help him, to provide for him a guide to the way of holiness by intellect and knowledge, like Khalkhal and Darda, and among the sages of truth a sage and an artisan, like Ethan and Heman, for perhaps the rabbis who lack this wisdom are to us false oracles and misleading ones, God forbid. And you, my lord, to you its secrets are revealed, and your treasure will fill the bellies of your disciples, they will be sated and delight in your goodness, and upon us to pay the wages of your work. And you, do not withhold good from its owners. And here I adjure you by the God of heaven: make Your face shine upon us, to answer the weary with a word spoken in its proper setting, and we shall be servants to my lord. And our lips will ask a great reward for your goodness, then we shall not be ashamed, neither in this world nor in the world to come, and we shall return and graze among the lilies from the company of sages and discerning ones.

tokens.note: אלוה: the singular Eloah, used of the one God (Deut 32:15; Job 3:4); rendered "God". הראשון, "the first", is the author's word, as the rabbis use it for the Creator before all that exists.
צמצם: 'contracted'. The tzimtzum (contraction) is the Kabbalists' doctrine; the English keeps the word fixed.
Partzuf (plural partzufim): a Kabbalistic entity; in the generic sense it means 'face'.
Literally 'creator of the beginning'. The Hebrew word is also the first word of Genesis.
תצוק: from יצק, "pour"; the phrase echoes Ps 41:9 (דְּבַר בְּלִיַּעַל יָצוּק בּוֹ), "a thing of Belial is poured upon him".
Belial: a Biblical word for worthlessness, here 'a word of Belial'.

השכל: hifil infinitive, "to have insight"; with וידוע it recalls Jer 9:23, "that he has insight and knows Me". The sentence says: who has gathered grace and good sense in his palms, in order to have insight and know the LORD.
Khalkhal: one of the four wise men named in 1 Kings 5:11.
Ethan: one of the four wise men named in 1 Kings 5:11.
Heman: one of the four wise men named in 1 Kings 5:11.

משאות: "burdens" or "oracles" (משא); the phrase is Lam 2:14 (מַשְּׂאוֹת שָׁוְא וּמַדּוּחִים), said of false prophecies that led astray. The sense: the rabbis who lack this wisdom are, for us, false and misleading guides.
לעות את יעף דבר (Isa 50:4): the verb is hard; here read "to answer the weary with a word"; others "to sustain the weary with a word".
Literally 'its wheels' (אפניו, written as in the source). The idiom means 'its proper setting'.
Song 2:16: the one who grazes among the lilies.

grammar: אמרו שאין ראוי is indirect speech ('said that it is not fitting'), so the segment has no quotation marks; the four infinitives that follow are its objects.
ולמה נניח ... ונעבוד ...? is a rhetorical question in first-person plural imperfects (not cohortatives: no ה ending); the Hebrew closes it with '?'.
מי יעלה בהר ה' and כי בער אנכי מאיש are embedded verses (Ps 24:3; Prov 30:2) with no quotation marks; their imperfects keep the verses' future sense.
הביננו אדונינו נלכה נרדפה: an imperative with a vocative ('our lord'), then a true cohortative pair ('let us go and pursue', after Hos 6:3).
ישבע ויתענגו are imperfects after תמלא and read as a result: 'they will be sated and delight'.
המצטמצם is a hitpael present participle ('that contracts'), and השכל וידוע is the infinitive pair of Jer 9:23 ('to have insight and to know').
segments.note: The questioner's letter, in his voice, addressed to the respondent as 'my lord'. Biblical phrases are embedded and unmarked.

segments.english: Second Reply. I saw all that is written in the letter of the eminent one, a tree whose branches are many, its height like the height of cedars, After the pardon for the delay, for the pressure of the times is outstretched, and every delay is for good. When I looked at the letter, behold, you opened your mouth, by mentioning divinities, thinking that it is against us. And what are we, that you murmur against us, and your scorn does not reach us, but only to the sages of Israel, whose least is thicker than your loins, and all Israel rests on them, and by their merit the world stands. Woe to you, for you have brought out against them words that are not according to the law, in innocence, and in its place guile. But your judgment has already been made clear, by the mouth of all the masters of wisdom. And as for what you wrote about Kisse Eliyahu, that on folio 3 he likens His oneness, may He be blessed, to the other unities. You are already walking in darkness. Surely the beginning of his words on folio 20 is that all these likenesses are about holy lights, which have no grasp, no form and no likeness, neither in intellect nor in knowledge at all and in principle, but so that the intellect can receive them, we were permitted to liken. And on folio 4b he wrote that all the epithets and attributes are in the manner of likeness, in the sefirot and the holy lights, the emanated beings. But in Him, may He be blessed, there is not in Him any likeness and form, and grasp in thought at all and in principle. And as for what you wrote, how can we leave the other partzufim and worship Ze'ir Anpin with the power in him, Ein Sof, blessed be He. The Master, Kisse Eliyahu, has already explained on folio 25b, that when we call upon Ze'ir Anpin, we call all the partzufim together, with a soul hidden in them. And as for what you wrote, why do we leave the partzufim closest to Ein Sof and call upon Ze'ir Anpin. Because it is known that among the inner attributes some are judgment and some are mercy, and this one includes them all, and therefore the Emanator wanted to perform His actions through this vessel. Before you object to the likenesses concerning the upper ones, which you have no right to ponder, all the more so to mock, object to your corporeal hand, which does all the labors, and the head above does not do anything. Also, the power of speech, which is your glory, above every living creature, why was it not given above your eyes. But thus His wisdom decreed, may He be blessed. And if you have proper counsel, go to your Creator and counsel Him. And as for what you wrote, that the words of Kisse Eliyahu are against the Rambam, etc., who wrote that it is not a force in a body, and according to the words of Kisse Eliyahu it is a force in a body. Surely all the Kabbalists with one mouth answer and say that whoever ascribes corporeality to the sefirot, like you, is a denier and has no share in the God of Israel. And as for their having called them subtle lights, it is only to soothe the ear! We have to ask about what the Rambam wrote: "Let him direct his heart toward the Shekhinah and pray." And in the Guide he wrote that the Shekhinah is a created light. And more than this, what he wrote about the glory of the LORD, that it is created. If so, how did Israel go out to the opening of their tents and bow down to the created thing. And more than this, what he wrote, that every form which the prophets saw and spoke with is a created light. If so, we have no prophecy through the Creator, but all of it from the side of the created ones. And if it is said that the created thing was attached to the Creator, then, in your opinion, it is a force in a body! Your answer will quickly spring up, the end of the verse: "They refuse to know Me, says the LORD."

tokens.note: Counted here, so 'divinities'; the abstract is 'divinity'.
תלינו: printed so; Exod 16:7 reads תלונו, "you murmur" (from לון). The English follows the verse; the printed word is in `apparatus`.
Kisse Eliyahu: the book, named in full here; the Hebrew title means 'the throne of Elijah'. First occurrence in the unit.
Folio 20, as the author gives it.
Folio 4 side b (ד' ע"ב): 4b.
ואודות: printed so ("and concerning"); read as ואורות, "and lights", after אורות קדושים (2:7.108). If אודות is kept: "and concerning the holy emanated beings".
Ze'ir Anpin, 'Small Face' (see 2:5.11).
הר': הרב, "the Master"; Kisse Eliyahu is the title of the book, used for its author (as הר' המורה for the Rambam).
כס"א: Kisse Eliyahu, named in full at 2:7.85.
Folio 25 side b (כ"ה ע"ב): 25b.
ועד שאתה מקשה ... תקשה: "before you object to ..., object to ..." (in the idiom, "instead of objecting to X, object to Y").
ותיעצנו: 2nd person masculine imperfect with the suffix -נו: "you will counsel him" (energic nun) or "counsel us". Read here "counsel Him".
וכו': 'etc.', kept as the Hebrew marks a truncated passage.
Moreh Nevukhim (the Guide for the Perplexed); the Hebrew names it only as 'the Guide' (במורה).
כ': כתב, "wrote" (not a chapter number); the Guide is named without a reference.
ס': read as סוף, "end" (the words close Jer 9:5); not certain. Other expansions: ספר, סימן.

and according to the words of Kisse Eliyahu it is a force in a body.
phrases.literal: and-according-to the-words-of Kisse-Eliyahu it-is a-force in-a-body

phrases.english: Surely all the Kabbalists
with one mouth
answer and say
that whoever ascribes corporeality to the sefirot, like you,
is a denier
and has no share in the God of Israel.
And as for their having called them
subtle lights,
it is only to soothe
the ear!
We have to ask
about what the Rambam wrote:
"Let him direct his heart toward the Shekhinah and pray."
And in the Guide he wrote
that the Shekhinah is a created light.
And more than this,
what he wrote about
the glory of the LORD, that it is created.
If so,
how did Israel go out
to the opening of their tents
and bow down to the created thing.
And more than this,
what he wrote,
that every form
which the prophets saw and spoke with
is a created light.
If so,
we have no prophecy
through the Creator,
but all of it from the side of the created ones.
And if it is said that
the created thing was attached to the Creator,
then, in your opinion, it is a force in a body!
Your answer will quickly spring up,
the end of the verse: "They refuse to know Me, says the LORD."

grammar: תשובה שנית is a heading ('Second Reply'): Chapter 2 is a correspondence, and the writer now answers the questioner in the second person (פערת פיך, כנגדינו).
אילן שענפיו מרובים, רומו כגובה ארזים is an image in apposition to כתב האלוף. Its last phrase alludes to Amos 2:9 and is unmarked.
Each 'ומה שכתבת' clause answers one point of the questioner's letter, in the order he gave them.
שכתב הרמב"ם: יכוין לבו כנגד השכינה ויתפלל is an explicit quotation with the formula 'wrote', so it takes double quotation marks; the Hebrew colon is kept.
ותשובתך מהרה תצמח alludes to Isa 58:8 and takes no marks. ס' מאנו דעת אותי נאם ה' is a quoted verse with the abbreviation ס' before it, so it takes quotation marks.
segments.note: The respondent's reply, in his voice. The Kabbalistic terms and the book's abbreviations follow the decisions for the work.
apparatus: Jer 9:5 (closing words, quoted): מאנו דעת אותי נאם ה'.
Isa 58:8 (allusion): ארכתך מהרה תצמח.
Amos 2:9 (allusion): אשר גבהו כגובה ארזים.
Folio numbers (3, 20, 4b, 25b) are the author's own; no reference is added.
Exod 16:7 (allusion): ונחנו מה כי תלונו עלינו; the base text prints תלינו, and the English follows the verse.
1 Kings 12:10 (allusion; also 2 Chr 10:10): קטני עבה ממתני אבי; the author writes קטנם עבה ממתניך.
Isa 50:10 (allusion): אשר הלך חשכים.
Exod 33:10 (allusion): ויקומו ... איש פתח אהלו והשתחוו.
2:7.141: the base text prints ואודות; the English reads ואורות (cf. אורות קדושים, 2:7.108).
2:7.397: ס' not expanded in the text; read as סוף (end of the verse); ספר or סימן are the alternatives.
Wikisource base text; not yet collated with the 1931 scan (Q2).
